analysis:
Examined units are documentation only. docs/architecture/inference.md head 1640-2266 is unchanged surrounding text (the file's only changed range is head 1030-1047, outside these units, per file_changes). That range describes a new in-process PromptTokenCache (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/PromptTokenCache.swift) that reuses token IDs of previously seen prompt pieces "in the same prefix-cache scope", with parallel encoding, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma4/GPT-OSS, a load-time comparison, sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on mismatch, and a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. docs/developer/test.md head 322-345 adds a test/benchmark section (PromptTokenCacheTests, ChatTemplateLoopRewritesTests, InboundChatRequestDecodeTests, ServeLoopColdLoadTests, darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep). No source code is in this batch, so no concrete regression is cited.

Integration questions (T-041/SEC-035, A-001, TB-007, T-028): (1) the token-ID cache retains plaintext-derived prompt pieces in memory; verify that it is keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt/cacheScope and is never shared across accounts, that it has bounded size/lifetime, and that it is never persisted to disk; that would add an at-rest surface outside KVCacheSSD HMAC protections. (2) Reuse hit/miss adds a CPU-side TTFT timing signal; within scope this matches the accepted same-account SEC-035 risk, but cross-scope keying must be verified in source. (3) Standalone/local mode scope semantics are unclear. (4) Correctness: rewritten templates or piecewise tokenization diverging from the canonical path could alter prompts (T-007-like integrity), mitigated by the sampled comparisons. (5) The merged inbound body decode (InboundChatRequestDecode) changes admission parsing; it must reject the same inputs as the separate decoders. (6) Cold-load parking in the serve loop is availability-related. The threat model T-041 does not mention this new prompt-token cache; consider a threat-model update once source is reviewed.
